title: An independent-date correction changed four British moth timing variance slopes by less than two percent in 1993-2015
abstract: We tested whether finite-catch error could explain spring warmth slopes of between-taxon mean capture-date variance. We used 117 consecutive trap-year pairs from England and Scotland in two periods in 1993-2015. An exact correction under independent capture dates changed all four equal-individual slopes by less than two percent. Corrected English slopes were +79.24 and +76.73 days squared per degree C; both four-test intervals were above zero. Scottish intervals included zero. Stricter filters weakened early England. Shared-night effects, capture bias, seasonal truncation and selected taxa remain unresolved. This diagnostic uses the same records as a prior campaign result and a related outcome without monthly effort weights. It does not identify a causal climate effect. Code, aggregate evidence, source hashes, a figure and retrieval instructions are included. External records remain outside the package.

display.caption: Spring warmth slopes for equal-individual date variance, an independent-date correction and the corrected outcome. Intervals adjust four tests within each outcome. The correction does not estimate shared-night effects.
